## Hinge question · Use the properties {#fv1-hinge .fv-lesson }

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="1" class="hinge numeric-choices"><p class="hinge-question">For arbitrary vectors, which expression is always equal to <span data-math="(2\underset{\sim}{a})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{c})"></span>?</p><div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:00</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option>30</option><option>45</option><option selected>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div><div class="choices"><button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span data-math="2(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b})+2(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{c})"></span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span data-math="2(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b})+\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{c}"></span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span data-math="4(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b})+4(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{c})"></span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span data-math="2(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b})(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{c})"></span></button></div><div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly.<br>On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div><div class="hinge-explanation" hidden><strong>1.</strong> Distribute the dot product, then take out the scalar factor from both terms.</div></div>
```

::: {.notes}
Correct answer: 1. (2a)·(b+c)=(2a)·b+(2a)·c=2(a·b)+2(a·c). Choice 2 applies the scalar factor only to the first term. Choice 3 treats doubling one vector as doubling both dot-product factors. Choice 4 turns a sum into a product. Start with a fist on chest, think quietly, and show 1–4 fingers together only on the teacher’s verbal cue. Default 60 seconds; timer expiry never reveals the answer. Ready: proceed to Example 1.1 and name the properties used. Divided: allow 30 seconds to compare reasoning with a partner, then vote again. Needs explanation: return to 2x(y+z), map back to the vector expression, and recheck.
:::
